newsitem.title: UK: Tesco Christmas/NY sales rise 7.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tesco Christmas/NY sales rise 7.5 pct.

text.p: British food retailing giant Tesco Plc said on Monday that its same-store sales in the five weeks covering the 1996 Christmas and New Year holidays rose by 7.5 percent in what it called "another excellent trading period".

In the 21 weeks to January 5 this year its like-for-like sales rose by 8.1 percent and chairman Lord MacLaurin said in a statement the supermarket group's sales "continued to outperform the industry average".
The company said its performance was the result of its trading strategy of "investing in low prices" after the launch of its Unbeatable Value campaign last September.
Tesco also said its product range and customer service approaches had borne fruit.
The company's Clubcard loyalty scheme had continued to grow in popularity and in November it awarded 56 million pounds ($94 million) worth of vouchers and money-off coupons to customers.
In his comments, MacLaurin's sole remark on profitability was that the company "looked forward to reporting another good set of results in April".
